title: Coherent cotensor exchange for equivalence nerves
statement:
Let $\mathcal V$ be presentably monoidal and use the algebroids and universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Use the spatial action $\diamond$, its right cotensors $C^K$, and the indiscrete algebroids $E^n_{\mathcal V},E^n_{\mathcal S}$ on $n+1$ objects of [lem-coef-algebroid-categorical-homotopy]. Here $\mathcal S$ is spaces with cartesian tensor. For a $\mathcal V$-algebroid $C$, put $I_p(C)=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)}(E^p_{\mathcal V},C)$ and $I(C)=|I_\bullet(C)|$ as in [lem-coef-algebroid-equivalence-nerve], where bars mean small geometric realization in spaces. Put $D_q=C^{E^q_{\mathcal S}}$. For all $p,q\geq0$ there are natural equivalences
$$I_p(D_q)\simeq I_q(C^{E^p_{\mathcal S}}).$$
They form an equivalence of bisimplicial spaces with the two directions exchanged, natural in $C$ and compatible with every simplicial operator. In particular they induce natural equivalences
$$|I_p(D_\bullet)|\simeq I(C^{E^p_{\mathcal S}}).$$
Let $a_p:C\to C^{E^p_{\mathcal S}}$ be induced by the collapse $E^p_{\mathcal S}\to E^0_{\mathcal S}$. Under the preceding identifications, the map $|I_0(D_\bullet)|\to|I_p(D_\bullet)|$ induced by $E^p_{\mathcal V}\to E^0_{\mathcal V}$ corresponds to $I(a_p):I(C)\to I(C^{E^p_{\mathcal S}})$, and is an equivalence. No completeness hypothesis on $C$ and no symmetric monoidal hypothesis on $\mathcal V$ is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 5.6.2, completeness square: the equivalences iota_1(C^{E^n}) = Map(E^1 tensor E^n,C) = iota_n(C^{E^1}) and identification of the left vertical map; the same argument with p in place of 1, using Corollary 4.3.17, Lemma 5.5.7 and Proposition 5.3.6. Read the retained GH.html source, arXiv:1312.3178v4. Not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this operadic infinity-category result.

proof.text: Write $P=[p]$ and $Q=[q]$, viewed only as finite discrete object spaces. By the spatial-action formula, $A_{p,q}=E^p_{\mathcal V}\diamond E^q_{\mathcal S}$ has objects $(i,j)\in P\times Q$ and every mapping object is $*\odot\mathbf1\simeq\mathbf1$; its compositions and units are the unit constraints. The same description holds for $B_{q,p}=E^q_{\mathcal V}\diamond E^p_{\mathcal S}$ on $Q\times P$. Define $t_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to B_{q,p}$ by $(i,j)\mapsto(j,i)$ and the identity on every unit mapping object. In the defining operadic diagrams this sends a string $((i_0,j_0),\ldots,(i_r,j_r))$ to $((j_0,i_0),\ldots,(j_r,i_r))$, retaining the order of the $r$ unit factors. Hence it commutes with each inert restriction, composition and unit insertion, including their coherences. The same rule is its inverse. For finite-set maps $f:P\to P'$ and $g:Q\to Q'$, both composites of the naturality square send $(i,j)$ to $(g(j),f(i))$ and have identity unit maps. Thus the $t_{p,q}$ are an equivalence of the two coherent diagrams, with their parameters exchanged; no permutation of tensor factors of $\mathcal V$ is involved.

source.place: Theorem 5.6.2, completeness-square tensor exchange; finite indiscrete construction of Definition 5.1.1 and spatial action of Corollary 4.3.17

proof.text:
Apply the natural cotensor adjunction twice, using $t_{p,q}$ between them:
$$I_p(C^{E^q_{\mathcal S}})\simeq\operatorname{Map}(A_{p,q},C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(B_{q,p},C)\simeq I_q(C^{E^p_{\mathcal S}}).$$
The middle equivalence is precomposition with $t_{p,q}^{-1}$. The outside equivalences are those of the mapping-space bifunctors in the cited adjunction, not separate choices in each bidegree. Step 1 gives their middle comparison as a transformation of coherent diagrams. Consequently the composite is natural in $C$ and in both finite-set parameters. Restricting those parameters to the simplex category proves compatibility with every face, degeneracy and their higher coherence, and yields the required equivalence of bisimplicial spaces with exchanged directions.

source.place: Corollary 4.3.17 and Definition 4.3.18; Theorem 5.6.2, displayed equivalences in the final completeness paragraph, with p in place of 1

proof.text:
Fix $p$ and regard step 2 as a coherent transformation of simplicial spaces indexed by $q$. It is an equivalence in that functor category by the vertexwise-equivalence criterion of the cited functor-cone calculus; therefore it has a coherent inverse. Realizing the two transformations gives inverse maps: the composites are identities because the colimit construction takes the two inverse homotopies to homotopies. Equivalently, precomposing cocones with these inverse transformations gives inverse equivalences of their cocone categories, carrying initial objects to initial objects. We obtain
$$|I_p(D_\bullet)|\simeq|I_\bullet(C^{E^p_{\mathcal S}})|=I(C^{E^p_{\mathcal S}}).$$
Here the realization on the right is precisely the one in the equivalence-nerve statement, so it exists under the stated smallness convention; the equivalent diagram on the left has a colimit by the cocone argument. The indexing category is the small simplex category, and all the spaces are the small mapping spaces stipulated in the item. The construction is natural in $C$ and in $p$ because step 2 was a transformation in those parameters as well.

source.place: Theorem 5.6.2, final completeness paragraph: passage from the simplicial exchange to geometric realization; expanded universal-property argument

proof.text: Let $s_p:E^p\to E^0$ be collapse, with its indicated enrichment in each occurrence. The map in the item before realization, in degree $q$, is precomposition by $s_p\diamond1:A_{p,q}\to A_{0,q}$. Under the swaps of step 1 it becomes $1\diamond s_p:B_{q,p}\to B_{q,0}$: both composite maps send $(i,j)$ first to the remaining coordinate $j$, and all their unit mapping maps are identities. Under the natural adjunction of step 2, precomposition by $1\diamond s_p$ is postcomposition by $C^{s_p}:C^{E^0_{\mathcal S}}\to C^{E^p_{\mathcal S}}$. Identify $C^{E^0_{\mathcal S}}\simeq C$ by the cited unit-cotensor equivalence. Thus this map is exactly $I_q(a_p)$. These comparisons are coherent in $q$ by the same finite-set naturality square. Realizing gives exactly $I(a_p)$ under step 3, including the source identification $|I_0(D_\bullet)|\simeq I(C)$ obtained by setting $p=0$.

source.place: Theorem 5.6.2, identification of the left vertical map in the completeness square; explicit collapse-coordinate calculation

proof.text: Both $[p]$ and $[0]$ are nonempty finite sets, even when $p=0$. The finite-set assertion of the categorical-homotopy node makes $s_p:E^p_{\mathcal S}\to E^0_{\mathcal S}$ a categorical equivalence. Its cotensor assertion therefore makes $C^{s_p}$ a categorical equivalence of $\mathcal V$-algebroids. Using the unit identification, the same holds for $a_p$. That node also says that every categorical equivalence is fully faithful and essentially surjective. Apply the equivalence-nerve node's assertion that a fully faithful essentially surjective functor induces an equivalence on $I$. It gives that $I(a_p)$, and hence the realized map in step 4, is an equivalence. Only presentable monoidality of $\mathcal V$ was used for the action and cotensor results; neither this application nor the nerve criterion requires $C$ to be complete or $\mathcal V$ to be symmetric monoidal.
